places.chef: 嶋 勇也 (Shima Yuya) · Owner, Head Roaster, Coffee Competition Judge · 名古屋市中区丸の内（2017年6月開業） · Born in Nagoya in 1982, Shima Yuya dreamed of running a coffee shop from childhood. After culinary school and stints at Italian restaurants and coffee shops around Aichi, he joined the long-established Kato Coffee (加藤珈琲店) in Nagoya, where he immersed himself in specialty coffee, and later studied roasting at a Gifu roastery. Hungry to go deeper, he moved to Melbourne — a world coffee capital — where he submitted roughly 50 résumés before landing his first café job. The experience sharpened both his barista skills and his sense of what a single cup can mean. He returned to Nagoya and opened Q.O.L. COFFEE in June 2017. · Q.O.L. stands for Quality of Life. Shima believes that a great cup of coffee can elevate everyday living — clothing, food, shelter — and sources world-grade specialty beans, visiting farms and serving as a competition judge to honor each producer's intention. · Self-roasted specialty drip coffee — approximately 10 bean varieties roasted on a Giesen W6A semi-hot-air (6kg) roaster; also known for its sandwiches, including a thick-cut egg sandwich.

places.chef: Family-run artisan tofu producer, Takeout stall operator · Nagoya, Aichi (Owari region), founded 1934 · 河口とうふ (Kawaguchi Tofu) was founded in 1934 in the Owari region of Nagoya, which has long been prized for its high-quality groundwater and proximity to premium soybean-growing areas. The family has made tofu using the same core principles for over 90 years: carefully selected domestic (non-GMO) soybeans, natural sea salt nigari as the coagulant, and local well water — never additives or shortcuts. The Kinshachi Yokocho stall opened when the castle-gate food arcade launched as part of the Nagoya Castle precinct redevelopment. · No GMOs, no additives, minimal intervention: the shop's philosophy is that great tofu needs only great soybeans, pure water, and natural nigari. The Owari region's terroir is central to their identity. · Tofu soft serve (豆腐ソフト) — a dense, subtly sweet soft-serve made from concentrated soy milk; the gold-leaf version (¥990) is the flagship tourist order. Tofu dengaku skewers (田楽, ¥500) — blocks of firm housemade tofu grilled and brushed with Hatcho-style sweet miso — are the deeper local eat.
places.gfd: The shop's tofu is made from soybeans, natural sea salt nigari, and well water — no wheat. Critically, the dengaku miso sauce is Hatcho-style (八丁味噌/豆味噌), which is brewed from soybeans and salt only — no wheat, unlike most soy sauces or rice/barley miso. This is a meaningful GF positive. However: (1) the soft serve cone/wafer almost certainly contains wheat — ask for a cup; (2) no dedicated GF certification exists; (3) the shared kitchen/counter of a busy market stall carries cross-contamination…

places.chef: 岡村菜穂子 (Naco Okamura) · Owner, Gluten-Free Advisor, GF community organiser (Instagram, Facebook, LINE) · Nishi-ku, Nagoya, Aichi (Joshin / 浄心) · Naco developed a wheat allergy as an adult and experienced first-hand the isolation of being unable to share meals with friends and family. Determined that no one should have to give up the pleasure of eating together, she trained as a gluten-free advisor and founded 株式会社テマトジカン (Tematojikan Co., Ltd.). みちのり弁当 opened January 27, 2023, in a lovingly repurposed 60-year-old wooden building in the Joshin (浄心) neighborhood — chosen to reduce demolition waste, with reclaimed wood and a transparent glass front that lets passersby see into the kitchen. · 「小麦アレルギーの人も、そうでない人も、一緒に食卓を囲み同じ食事で『おいしいね』を分かち合う」— People with and without wheat allergies can sit at the same table and share the joy of 'this is delicious.' · Rice-flour karaage bento (米粉唐揚げ) — the shop's signature, chicken fried in a rice-flour coating, prepared wheat-free
places.gfd: Tokai region's first dedicated gluten-free bento shop. Wheat, barley, rye, and oats are excluded from all ingredients including seasonings and condiments. places.chef: Nishimura Kazunori (西村 和則) · chain restaurant, chicken specialist, Nagoya Cochin showcase, Nagoya Castle tourism anchor · Nagoya, Aichi — founded at Nagoya Station West Exit 2000; Kinshachi Yokocho branch opened in the Yoshinao (Gishoku) Zone of the castle precinct. · Nishimura Kazunori grew up in an Ise-Shima fishing town with a fisherman father. Despite those coastal roots, it was chicken — specifically the joy of biting into wings at childhood Christmas dinners — that became his culinary north star. In 2000 he opened a small ~10-tsubo (about 33 sq m) izakaya called Torikai at Nagoya Station's west exit, serving yakitori, tebasaki and karaage. The turning point came at the 2005 Aichi Expo, where he ran a booth selling both branded Nagoya Cochin and unbranded chicken side by side: despite a price difference of nearly 10x, diners overwhelmingly chose the Nagoya Cochin. That moment convinced him that quality provenance could command loyalty. In 2007 he incorporated as Progre Corp. and rebranded as Torikai Sohonke, pivoting the menu to centre on oyakodon and tebasaki made with Nagoya Cochin. The Kinshachi Yokocho branch, opened inside the tourism precinct at Nagoya Castle's main gat…
places.gfd: The restaurant uses standard wheat-containing soy sauce in both the tebasaki wing sauce and the oyakodon tare. No gluten-free options, dedicated fryer, or allergen-substitution program are documented anywhere. Celiac-unsafe; avoid.
places.vgd: Entirely a chicken-specialist restaurant. Every dish centres on Nagoya Cochin or domestic chicken. places.chef: cafe operator · Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture · The kissashitsu operates inside the Nagoya City Archives building (名古屋市市政資料館), a striking Neo-Baroque brick structure completed in 1922 as the Nagoya Court of Appeals and District/Summary Court. The building served judicial functions until 1979, when it was repurposed as a civic archive and designated an Important Cultural Property. The cafe occupies a former courtroom (第貳號法廷) on an upper floor, its retro character preserved largely intact. · Unhurried, inexpensive refreshment in a space that doubles as living history — visitors rest among marble staircases, stained-glass windows and the quiet hum of an archive. The cafe makes no effort to modernize; its retro character is the point. · ミックスサンド (mixed sandwich, ¥600) pairing cucumber, tomato and potato salad, alongside 小倉トースト (ogura/red-bean toast) — a nod to Nagoya's red-bean toast tradition — and hand-drip coffee.

places.vgd: Menu is simple kissaten fare: mixed sandwiches (egg, ham, potato salad fillings), ogura toast, and coffee. No dedicated vegan options; most sandwiches contain egg and/or ham. No founding date or owner biography is publicly documented. · The kitchen prioritizes quality local chicken and grilling over high-heat binchotan charcoal on a custom extra-large grill to seal in natural umami, letting the ingredient speak rather than heavy seasoning. · Charcoal-grilled chicken skewers using Kinsou-dori (錦爽どり), an Aichi-area brand chicken, finished with a housemade salt blended from bonito and kombu dashi — no chemical additives.
places.gfd: Standard yakitori with no gluten-free declaration. Tare (dipping sauce) used on many skewers contains wheat-based soy sauce (shoyu). The house salt blend is made from bonito and kombu dashi and is advertised as additive-free, but wheat-free status is unconfirmed. Charcoal grilling reduces cross-contamination risk versus frying, but shared grills and shared prep areas are standard. No dedicated GF menu or allergen guide found on any source. Celiacs should ask about tare vs. shio (salt) options a…
places.vgd: This is a dedicated yakitori restaurant — the entire menu revolves around grilled chicken and offal. The house seasoning salt is made from bonito (katsuobushi) and kombu dashi, making even the salt-grilled items non-vegan. No plant-based skewer alternatives are offered. Vegetarians and vegans have essentially no options here beyond side salads or cold tofu if available, but these are not confirme…
places.hours: 17:30–22:30 (L.O. 22:00); closed Thu (some sources note irregular closures)

places.n: 鰻 木屋 (Unagi Kiya)
places.hood: 東区 東大手 (Higashi Ward, Higashi-Ote)
places.notes: [Mom & Pop] Founded in the late Edo period, Unagi Kiya is one of Nagoya's oldest surviving eel restaurants, now run by its fifth generation of ownership. It sits a short walk from Higashi-Ote Station in the historically layered Higashi Ward, not far from Nagoya Castle.
places.chef: fifth-generation family operation · Late Edo period, Nagoya · Founded in the late Edo period (江戸末期), Unagi Kiya is one of Nagoya's oldest surviving eel restaurants, now run by its fifth generation. It sits about a three-minute walk from Higashi-Ote Station in the historically layered Higashi Ward, not far from Nagoya Castle. · Simplicity and continuity: well water is still used to rest live eel before grilling, and the menu is kept deliberately short. · Unagi don (eel rice bowl) and ohitsu-mabushi — the house style features Kansai-influenced belly-split eel grilled directly over binchotan charcoal without steaming, producing a crisper exterior than Edo-style preparations. The thick-cut eel is sourced from Kagoshima, stored live in well water before service, and finished with a rich house tare.
places.gfd: Traditional unagi tare (kabayaki glaze) is made with standard wheat-containing soy sauce — a significant gluten source. Dashi used in soups is fish-based but likely made with standard ingredients. No GF claims on the menu or website. The restaurant does not advertise any allergen accommodations. Guests with celiac disease should call ahead (052-951-8781) and ask specifically about the soy sauce and tare; substitution is unlikely at a traditional specialist of this type. Cross-contamination risk…
places.vgd: Entirely eel-focused menu. All dishes built around unagi; soups are fish-based (鯉 or dashi); no plant-based options offered. Not suitable for vegans or vegetarians.
places.hours: Tue–Sat 11:00–13:30 (lunch only). Saturday dinner by full reservation only (around 17:30). Closed Sun, Mon, holidays, and on Doyō-no-ushi-no-hi (midsummer eel day).

places.n: ブランカ (gallery+cafe blanka)
places.hood: Marunouchi, Naka Ward (along the Horikawa; 5 min walk from Marunouchi Stn Exit 8)
places.notes: [Mom & Pop] A gallery cafe created by renovating the historic storehouse (kura) of Oki Masa Shoten, a lumber merchant founded in 1907 (Meiji 40). Located along the Horikawa, it is a rare space where gallery and cafe merge, characterized by high ceilings and the warmth of wood. Its three gallery spaces host contemporary-art exhibitions, pop-ups, readings and more.
places.chef: ギャラリー運営, カフェ・ビストロ · 愛知県名古屋市中区丸の内（堀川沿い） · 明治40年（1907年）創業の材木商・沖正商店が営む老舗の蔵をリノベーションして誕生したギャラリーカフェ。 堀川沿いに位置し、高い天井と木のぬくもりが特徴的な空間で、ギャラリーとカフェが一体となった稀有な場所。 3つのギャラリースペースでは現代アートの展覧会、ポップアップ、朗読会などが開催される。 · アートを身近に感じられる場所をつくりたいという想いから生まれた空間。 高知県嶺北地域の野菜や愛知県産の地場野菜を中心に、身体にやさしい素材を大切にしたビストロ料理を提供。 亜硫酸塩添加量を抑えたナチュラルワインも揃える。 · キッシュランチ（1日5食限定）／無農薬野菜たっぷりのサラダ
places.gfd: The main menu items — focaccia, quiche pastry and pasta — contain wheat. No explicit gluten-free accommodation. Whether soy sauce is used is unknown. No mention of a dedicated fryer or cross-contamination measures. Celiac accommodation cannot be expected; advance confirmation is essential.
places.vgd: Many menu items are vegetable-centered, but the mainstays include quiche (using egg and cream), focaccia and chiffon cake, which contain dairy and eggs. Lunch courses also feature pork (from Chita) and seafood. There is no explicit full-vegan accommodation, and whether a hidden dashi (bonito, dried sardine) is used is also unknown. Phoning to confirm in advance is strongly recommended.
places.hours: Tue–Sat 11:30–16:30 (lunch L.O. 14:00), 18:00–22:00 (dinner L.O. 21:00); Sun 11:30–16:30; closed Mon (also reportedly closed the first Tuesday of each month)

places.n: LIT（リト） (LIT (Rito))
places.hood: Kaminagoya, Nishi Ward / 10 min walk from Joshin Stn
places.notes: [Mom & Pop] Originally started as the spice-curry 'LIT COFFEE,' it then spent about three years serving ankake pasta from a food truck at events nationwide. On January 12, 2026 it opened a permanent shop in an alley in Kaminagoya, Nishi Ward, Nagoya. The horse in the shop's logo evokes an 'image of moving about freely'; the New Year opening also coincided with 'the timing of the Year of the Horse.'
places.chef: オーナーシェフ（名前非公開） · 名古屋市西区上名古屋 · もともとスパイスカレーの「LIT COFFEE」として出発し、その後約3年間キッチンカーであんかけパスタを各地のイベントで提供してきた。 2026年1月12日、名古屋市西区上名古屋（浄心駅近く）の路地に実店舗をオープン。 店のロゴに馬をあしらったのは「自由に動き回るイメージ」から。 年明けの開業は「午年のタイミング」とも重なった。 · キッチンカー時代の熱量をそのまま実店舗に持ち込む、移動する食の精神。 レトロ喫茶の雰囲気の中で、名古屋めしのあんかけパスタを真剣に掘り下げる。 · あんかけスパゲッティ（S200g/M300g/L400g・20種以上のトッピングから選択可）。 看板はフィッシュプレート：揚げた白身魚に野菜の甘みを引き出したマイルドなあんかけソースをかけたもので、塩気と甘みのバランスが特徴とされる。
places.gfd: Ankake spaghetti is built around wheat-flour noodles, and there is no mention whatsoever of gluten-free accommodation. It should be regarded as unsuitable for celiacs or those with wheat allergy.
places.vgd: The signature offerings are seafood dishes such as the fish plate, and while the sauce is described as a mild, vegetable-based umami, there is no explicit vegan accommodation. Whether any meat- and fish-free option exists is unknown, so confirmation before visiting is needed.
places.hours: Tue–Wed and Sat–Sun 11:30–15:00 (L.O. 14:30); Thu also open evenings 18:00–20:00 (L.O. 19:30); closed Mon and Fri. Occasional temporary closures (check Instagram).

places.notes: [Mom & Pop] Born in December 1969 in Aichi Prefecture, Fujiwara trained for 16 years at the celebrated Osaka kaiseki restaurant Sakuichi (作一) before returning to Nagoya and opening ふじ原 in 2004. The restaurant relocated and was fully renovated in 2016 to its current third-floor home inside th
places.chef: 藤原光章 (Fujiwara Mitsuaki) · owner-chef · Aichi Prefecture (Nagoya), trained in Osaka · Born in December 1969 in Aichi Prefecture, Fujiwara trained for 16 years at the Osaka Japanese restaurant Sakuichi (作一) before returning to Nagoya and opening ふじ原 in 2004. The restaurant relocated and was fully renovated in 2016 to its current third-floor home inside the White Mates building near Hisaya-Odori. · Fujiwara says he works so as never to 'bring shame to the name of Sakuichi,' where he learned his fundamentals — a commitment to thorough, quality work inherited from his Osaka training. He emphasises seasonal ingredients and wants guests to feel they can speak up casually about what they'd like to eat, making high-end kappo feel approachable. · Seasonal kappo-style Japanese cuisine rooted in Osaka (Naniwa-ryori) tradition: a rotating à la carte board of over 100 items, including a seasonal sashimi assortment (toro, sawara, ribbonfish, red seabream, squid and more), wild eel grilled two ways (white-grilled shirayaki and sauce-glazed / うなぎの二色焼), and steamed sweet bream with bamboo shoot (甘鯛の若竹蒸し).
places.gfd: Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is a foundational ingredient in kappo cooking at this level. Wheat appears in soy sauce marinades, tare, and likely in many braised and simmered preparations. Tempura is not prominent on documented menus, but shared prep surfaces and no dedicated GF protocols are documented. The chef is known for accommodating individual requests, so a celiac diner should communicate clearly at the time of reservation; however, the kitchen is not certified GF and c…
places.vgd: This is a traditional kappo restaurant built around seasonal seafood, fish-based dashi (likely katsuobushi/konbu blends), and standard Japanese soy sauce containing wheat. No vegan menu or plant-based options are advertised. Signature dishes include eel, sashimi, beef tendon, and sea urchin. A diner with advance notice might discuss a vegetable-forward arrangement with the chef — he has stated "p…
places.hours: Mon–Sat 17:30–22:00, closed Sun & holidays. No lunch service.

places.n: 金鯱寿司 (Kinshachi Zushi)
places.hood: Naka-ku, Ninomaru / Kinshachi Yokochō (1 min walk from Nagoyajō Stn)
places.notes: Muto grew up watching his father run a tonkatsu restaurant called Nabeyaki in Nagoya's Kita Ward. Initially reluctant to follow a culinary path, he was won over after spending one week helping his father and witnessing firsthand how much joy food brought to regular customers. Tha
places.chef: 武藤輝将 (Terumasa Muto) · オーナー (owner), 経営者 (operator), 寿司職人 (sushi chef at counter) · Muto grew up watching his father run a tonkatsu restaurant called なべや (Nabeya) in Nagoya's Kita Ward. Initially reluctant to follow a culinary path, he was won over after spending one week helping his father and witnessing firsthand how much joy food brought to regular customers. That experience drove him to pursue hospitality with a goal of reaching even more people than his father had. · Guard the best of traditional Edo-mae sushi while pursuing new challenges others haven't attempted — blending seasonal local ingredients (Mikawa large clams, Gifu Hatsushimo rice, Nagoya miso beef) with refined craftsmanship. · Creative Nagoya-style nigiri using both red and white vinegar for the shari, chosen strategically per ingredient; signature shrimp piece arranged to resemble Nagoya's golden kinshachi ornament.
places.gfd: Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used throughout; the menu features tempura (Mikawa clam tempura noted), shari rice seasoned with red and white vinegar (check for mirin), and dashi-based dishes — none of which are labelled gluten-free. No dedicated GF accommodation or tamari option is advertised anywhere. Celiac diners should call ahead and must ask specifically about soy sauce and hidden wheat in dashi and vinegar seasonings.
places.vgd: Entirely seafood and animal-product focused: nigiri, sashimi, chawanmushi (egg custard), crab cream croquette, eel, Nagoya miso-seasoned beef, and dashi-based preparations. No plant-based alternatives are offered or implied.

places.n: 二の丸茶亭 (Ninomaru Chatei)
places.hood: 中区 本丸 (Nakaku, Honmaru — inside Nagoya Castle)
places.notes: 二の丸茶亭 is a traditional tearoom operated by the Nagoya Castle Promotion Company (名古屋城振興株式会社) inside the grounds of Nagoya Castle, situated beside the designated scenic Ninomaru Garden — historically the garden of the Owari Tokugawa lords, the largest castle-lord residential garden
places.chef: City-affiliated tearoom operated by the Nagoya Castle Promotion Association (名古屋城振興協会) · 名古屋城内 二之丸庭園 (Ninomaru Garden, Nagoya Castle) · 二の丸茶亭 is a traditional tearoom operated in connection with the Nagoya Castle Promotion Association (名古屋城振興協会) inside the grounds of Nagoya Castle, situated beside the nationally designated scenic Ninomaru Garden — historically the garden of the Owari Tokugawa lords and, at roughly 30,000 square meters, the largest castle-lord residential garden in Japan. The tearoom serves visitors as an integrated rest stop within one of Japan's most-visited castle complexes. · A place to slow down mid-castle-visit and experience a moment of traditional tea culture, framed by a nationally designated scenic garden — the tearoom's ethos is quiet appreciation of season and setting rather than culinary ambition. · Matcha tea served with seasonal wagashi confections; gold-leaf matcha (金箔抹茶) is the premium signature offering
places.gfd: Pure matcha and most traditional wagashi (nerikiri mochi, mitsumame bean jelly) are rice- and bean-based and typically contain no wheat. However, the Gold Shachi Morning set includes toast (明確に小麦含む). No dedicated gluten-free kitchen, no allergen labeling, no staff allergy training confirmed. Cross-contamination risk is unknown. Celiac diners should stick to matcha with mitsumame or nerikiri and confirm ingredients on the day — avoid the morning toast set entirely.
places.vgd: Traditional wagashi (nerikiri, mitsumame) and plain matcha are typically free of meat, fish, and dairy — making them incidentally vegan in most cases. Mitsumame contains agar jelly, sweet azuki beans, and fruit, all plant-based. However, no vegan labeling exists, no confirmation that dashi or animal-derived additives are absent from sweets, and the Gold Shachi Morning toast almost certainly conta…
places.hours: 9:00–16:45 (last order 16:30); Gold Shachi Morning 9:00–11:00 limited qty daily; on the 8th of each month a formal tea ceremony is held and morning service is unavailable that day

places.n: カバッチ (Kabacchi)
places.hood: Marunouchi, Naka Ward (4 min walk from subway Marunouchi Stn Exit 8)
places.notes: Kabacchi is a Brazilian-cuisine cafe that opened on the 1st floor of the HP Marunouchi Building in Marunouchi, Nagoya in March 2026. Under a concept combining pesticide-free vegetables delivered directly from local farmers with traditional Brazilian dishes, it features a retro, cute interior that is easy for even a woman dining alone to enter.
places.chef: カフェ・レストラン · カバッチは2026年3月2日に名古屋・丸の内のHP丸の内ビル1階にオープンしたブラジル料理カフェ。農薬不使用・減農薬の地元農家直送野菜とブラジル伝統料理を組み合わせたコンセプトを掲げ、女性一人でも入りやすいレトロで可愛らしい内装が特徴。 · 化学調味料に頼らず素材本来の旨みを大切に。地元農家から届くオーガニック野菜と南米の家庭料理の知恵を融合し、体に寄り添う食事を提供する。 · ピカーニャ（ブラジル式300gステーキ）、ムケッカ（ブラジル伝統のココナッツミルクベースのシーフードシチュー）、姉妹店の牛タンを使った牛タンカレーランチ
places.gfd: The restaurant emphasizes organic, additive-free ingredients and avoids chemical seasonings, but makes no gluten-free claims. Brazilian-style stews and grills may involve wheat-containing soy sauce or marinades. No dedicated GF menu, no allergen labeling found online. Cross-contamination risk is unknown. Celiac diners should contact the restaurant directly before visiting.
places.vgd: The menu centers on Brazilian meat dishes (picanha steak, moqueca seafood stew, beef-tongue curry) with organic vegetables on the side. No dedicated vegan dishes are listed. Hidden animal-based broths and animal proteins are likely throughout. Ask staff before ordering.
places.hours: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:00 (L.O. 13:30), 18:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:30); closed Sat, Sun and public holidays

places.notes: [GF] Rice-flour cafe/bar (open Sep 2024) marketing GF ingredients, not a verified dedicated kitchen. A live bar pours barley beer/alcohol on the same premises and the 十割 buckwheat mazesoba sauce likely contains wheat soy sauce, so celiacs must ask about tamari, dedicated prep and cross-contact. places.chef: owner, operator · Nagoya, Aichi · Cafe&Bar REAL opened in September 2024 (13 Sept) on 太閤通 in Nakamura-ku, about a 3-minute walk from Taikodori Station. It is run by a singer-songwriter owner who focuses on gluten-free eating for health and built the shop around it. Lunch centres on a rice-flour hamburger with a house-baked bun and a 100%-pork binder-free patty, plus rice-flour cheesecake and scones; evenings run as a casual bar with drink-and-snack sets. Organic coffee/tea, non-caffeine and soy-milk options are offered. · 「美味しく、健康的に」— not compromising taste just because it is gluten-free (グルテンフリーだからといって味を妥協しない). · Rice-flour hamburger (自家製バンズ・豚肉100%パティ) and rice-flour pizza, with buns and pizza dough baked in-house
places.gfd: A singer-songwriter-run cafe/bar that opened Sep 2024, marketing itself as a 「グルテンフリー食材を使用したCafe＆Bar」/「名古屋・グルテンフリーカフェ」 with rice-flour burgers, pizza, cheesecake and scones. This is bare 'uses GF ingredients' marketing — the JP guide ashiya-obentofesta explicitly notes 「完全なグルテンフリー専門店であるかどうかは確認が取れていません」 (cannot confirm it is a complete gluten-free specialist) and no dedicated wheat-free-kitchen claim is published. Risk items remain: a functioning bar serves barley beer/alcohol on-site, buckwheat…
places.vgd: Not a vegan venue — 100% pork burger patties and dairy cheesecake feature. Soy-milk and non-caffeine drink options exist, so a few items may be adaptable; confirm case by case.
places.hours: Cafe 11:00–15:00 / bar 18:00–23:00 (Sat/Sun/holidays continuous 11:00–23:00) / closed Mon (if a holiday, closed the following Tue)

places.n: COrPO (やさしいスイーツカフェ COrPO)
places.hood: 中川区荒子 (Arako, Nakagawa-ku), Nagoya
places.cu: Gluten-free cafe — rice-flour bread, lunch plates, tarts & parfaits
places.notes: [GF-dedicated] Fully wheat-free cafe in Arako (4 min from Arako Station on the Aonami Line, ~13 min from Takahata subway). Everything sold — rice-flour breads, lunch plates and tarts — is gluten-free, and wheat flour is neither used nor allowed onto the premises, which makes it one of the safer celiac stops in western Nagoya. It runs in cooperation with a pastry shop (reported as Firenze/フィレンツェ), but the COrPO shop itself is wheat-free; still confirm frying and airborne-flour handling if you are highly sensitive. Closed Wednesdays; whole tarts/cakes need ~3 days' advance order.
places.chef: owner, pastry · Nagoya, Japan · COrPO opened in Arako, Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya as a gluten-free specialty cafe and bakery, run in cooperation with a local pastry shop reported by Nagoya food media as Firenze (フィレンツェ). The name COrPO is Italian for 'body' (身体), reflecting a body-kind, gut-friendly concept aimed at people with wheat allergy and those wanting to improve intestinal health. The shop's stated aim is an inclusive table where people with and without allergies can eat together without restriction, offering bread, lunches and sweets made without wheat flour or refined sugar and with an emphasis on organic ingredients. Individual owner/chef names are not published in Japanese sources reviewed. · 「身体に 家族に 地域にやさしい パン・スイーツのある食生活を提供するお店」 — food that is kind to body, family and community; wheat- and refined-sugar-free, organic-leaning, and inclusive of allergy and non-allergy diners alike. · 100% rice-flour (米粉) bread, gluten-free lunch plates, and seasonal fruit tarts/parfaits made without wheat flour or white sugar
places.gfd: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→high. places.vgd: Not a vegan venue. The menu centers on dairy, eggs and meat — roast pork, loco moco hamburger, shrimp, French toast, cream-topped crepes and tart cream. A few items lean plant-forward (e.g. the seasonal 夏野菜カレー summer-vegetable curry, and a kids' hamburger made without eggs using a miso binder), but none are confirmed fully vegan. Ask staff about a specific dish if you need it dairy/egg-free.

places.n: Creperiz Stand Nagoya (Creperiz Stand Nagoya)
places.hood: 中区大須 (Osu), Naka-ku, Nagoya — relocating near Nagoya Station
places.notes: [2026-08-19] The 大須 shop has closed; the stand is 移転準備中 toward the Nagoya Station area with no confirmed address or reopening date, and its Instagram has been quiet since Feb 2025. Confirm it exists before travelling. [GF] 100% rice-flour crepe stand — crepe batter AND custard cream are wheat-free (no wheat, oats or buckwheat). RELOCATION ALERT: the Osu shop (中区大須3-30-25 大信ビル 合点承知1階) is scheduled to close at the end of March 2026 for building seismic-reinforcement work, and the stand plans to reopen near Nagoya Station around mid-2026 — confirm current location and hours via Instagram @creperiz_sta.nagoya before visiting. Stand-only, takeout, no seating.
places.chef: owner, rice farmer · Rankoshi, Hokkaido (蘭越町) — 木村農園 rice farm · Creperiz Stand is run by the fifth generation of 木村農園, a long-established rice-farming family in Rankoshi, Hokkaido. They first opened the parent café 'cafe creperiz' in Hokkaido in March 2021 to showcase their own ゆめぴりか rice, then debuted the Nagoya stand in Osu (Naka-ku) on 7 February 2025. The concept is a 100% rice-flour crepe — including a rice-flour custard cream — made without wheat, oats or buckwheat so that people with wheat allergies can enjoy crepes. · Showcase the family's own Hokkaido rice by making crepes and cream entirely from rice flour, so that wheat-allergic customers can enjoy crepes with no wheat, oats or buckwheat. · 米粉100% crepes with rice-flour custard cream (e.g. いちごWクリーム strawberry double-cream)

places.n: en-kitchen cafe (エンキッチン)
places.hood: 中区大井町 (Higashi-Betsuin, Naka-ku, Nagoya)
places.notes: [GF-dedicated] Fully wheat-free vegetable cafe near Higashi-Betsuin station: no wheat flour is used anywhere, utensils are kept separate, and wheat flour is banned from the premises, so cross-contact risk is very low. Bread is rice-flour (米粉) based and all sweets are wheat/egg/dairy-free. (フジタセイカ株式会社) was founded on 8 December 1938 (昭和13年) when first-generation 藤田四郎 began making confectionery in Nakamura-ku, Nagoya. From 1978 (昭和53年) the second-generation and current president 藤田吉彦 began producing the shop's signature 栗せん — a wheat-free rice cracker made with white-bean paste and egg. Alongside 栗せん the factory long produced 動物ヨーチ (small animal biscuits, a wheat product); rising wheat prices and aging equipment led the company to end 動物ヨーチ in summer 2022 and pivot the entire operation to gluten-free manufacturing. The retail shop 菓子屋 藤ノ宮 opened on 23 September 2022 as the factory's direct-sales outlet. · 「小麦を使わないおいしいお菓子とパンを作っています」 — to make genuinely delicious sweets and bread entirely without wheat, carrying a legacy senbei craft into a fully gluten-free future. · 栗せん (wheat-free chestnut senbei with white-bean paste) and 100% rice-flour bread & 和洋折衷 sweets.

The plain 米粉100%食パン (rice flour, sugar, salt, yeast, vegetable oil) appears egg- and dairy-free, so a plant-based option exists — confirm the specific loaf, as flavored breads (cheese, etc.) are not vegan.

places.n: Kagome (香米豆ーkagomeー)
places.hood: 豊橋市杉山町 (Sugiyama-cho, Toyohashi City, Aichi)
places.notes: [GF-dedicated] A fully wheat-free, dairy-free and egg-free rice-flour bakery — safe for celiacs since no wheat is handled on site (「小麦の取り扱いなし」). Everything from the shokupan loaves to bagels and focaccia is GF; nothing to avoid on the shelf. Note the very limited schedule: open only Fri–Sun on the 2nd and 4th weekends of the month, mornings only, and popular items sell out shortly after the 7:30 open, so go early and/or reserve via Instagram or text.
places.chef: owner, baker · 豊橋市, 愛知県 (Toyohashi, Aichi, Japan) · Kagome is a small husband-and-wife bakery in a residential corner of Sugiyama-cho, Toyohashi. The wife bakes the breads while the husband runs the shopfront and its small attached gallery, which hosts rotating art exhibitions. The bakery was built specifically around allergen-free baking — using no wheat, dairy or egg — to serve people with allergies and those seeking gluten-free food. · To make gluten-free, allergen-friendly bread (no wheat/dairy/egg/refined white sugar) that is still genuinely delicious — famous locally for a 'surprisingly mochi-like' (驚くほどもっちり) rice-flour crumb — so that people with allergies can enjoy bakery bread safely. · Rice-flour shokupan (米粉食パン) leavened with Shirakami-kodama yeast (白神こだま酵母), plus rice-flour bagels, focaccia and oatmeal breads.

places.vgd: Every product is also dairy-free and egg-free (卵・乳製品不使用), and sweetening is done only with plant sources — きび砂糖 (cane sugar), 甜菜糖 (beet sugar) and メープルシロップ (maple syrup). No animal products are used across the range, so the bread, bagels and focaccia are effectively fully vegan. Honey is not listed; confirm individual seasonal baked sweets if strictly avoiding it.
places.hours: 7:30–13:30 (or until sold out); open Fri–Sun on the 2nd and 4th weekends of each month only. Morning eat-in set from 8:00.

places.n: Bakeshop SolSol (グルテンフリー米粉パン専門店 Bakeshop SolSol)
places.hood: 碧南市三宅町 (Miyakecho, Hekinan City), Aichi
places.notes: [GF-dedicated] 100% wheat-free rice-flour bakery — the owner opened it as a standalone shop expressly to separate the kitchen from any wheat baking, so the whole product line is celiac-oriented. Its 花酵母のカンパーニュ (flower-yeast campagne) swept the 2024 2nd Delicious Rice Flour Bread Contest (Grand Prix + Gluten-Free Award). Go early: they bake a fixed batch and close when sold out. Closed Mon & Tue.
places.chef: 片山幸寛 (Katayama Yukihiro) · owner, baker, store manager · Hekinan City, Aichi, Japan · Katayama Yukihiro founded Bakeshop SolSol in Hekinan City after his nephew was diagnosed with a wheat allergy and could no longer eat ordinary wheat bread. Rather than baking gluten-free bread alongside wheat, he deliberately opened as a standalone gluten-free specialty shop so the kitchen would never share equipment or airborne flour with wheat products. Drawing on more than 15 years of bread-making, he works exclusively with rice flour (including Koshihikari) and his own SolSol rice-flour blends. In 2024 his 花酵母のカンパーニュ (flower-yeast campagne) took the Grand Prix, the Gluten-Free Award and the consumer-voted 'My Rice Flour Bread' award — a triple crown — at the 2nd Delicious Rice Flour Bread Contest in Yamagata. · Make bread that people who cannot eat wheat can enjoy without compromise (小麦が食べられない人でも我慢せずに食べられるパン). · Flower-yeast rice-flour campagne (made with rare red-carnation flower yeast) and rice-flour breads/sweets, all wheat-free.
places.gfd: A dedicated gluten-free rice-flour bakery with no wheat on the premises. The shop states 「小麦パンと厨房を分けるために、専門店として独立開業しました」(we opened independently as a specialty shop specifically to keep our kitchen separate from wheat bread) and 「小麦粉アレルギーがある方でも安心して召し上がっていただけます」(safe for those with wheat-flour allergies to eat with peace of mind). The Japanese celiac guide jp.japan-glutenfree.com rates it ★★★★★ and confirms 「全ての商品に小麦を使っていません」(none of the products use wheat). Because it is 100% wheat-free with a …
places.vgd: Not a vegan bakery. Many items are dairy/egg-rich (cream bread, chocolate breads, custard, waffles), while some plain rice-flour loaves may be plant-based. No vegan labelling is published, so ask per item.
places.hours: Weekdays 11:00–17:00 / Weekends & holidays 11:00–18:00, closed Mon & Tue. May close early once the day's bread sells out.

places.n: Ve Tree (ヴィーツリー)
places.hood: 名古屋市北区鳩岡 (Hatooka, Kita-ku, along 国道41号 / Route 41, near Kurokawa)
places.cu: Vegan & gluten-free cakes, baked sweets and cookies (rice-flour / soy-flour)
places.notes: [GF-dedicated] Fully wheat-free vegan sweets shop — every cake and cookie is safe for celiacs since no wheat is used on premises. Retail is open Saturdays only (10:00–17:00); whole cakes must be reserved ~1 week ahead. Great for a safe dessert stop or gift box, but not a meal venue (sweets, plus a newer vegan rice-flour burger).
places.chef: 野口 亜希子 (Akiko Noguchi) · owner, representative, cooking instructor · Nagoya, Japan · Owner-representative 野口亜希子 founded the parent business VegeBio (ベジビーオ) as a healthy cooking studio on 2014-07-01, near Kurokawa station in Nagoya's Kita-ku. The name VegeBio combines 'Vegetable' and 'Biology,' reflecting her philosophy of building energetic, healthy daily life through vegetables and fruit. In 2017 the business expanded into retail and online sales, and after repeated customer requests to buy the cakes and baked goods from her classes, she opened the Ve Tree storefront (2022-01-11) as a dedicated vegan & gluten-free cake shop. The name 'Ve Tree' joins 'Ve' (vegan) with 'Tree,' symbolizing buds forming and blossoms appearing — growth. · That truly delicious food should also satisfy the body's needs and be sustainable; sweets are positioned as 'reward treats' (ご褒美) that enrich life and serve as an entry point for customers to reconsider their broader eating habits. · Vegan & gluten-free cakes and baked sweets made with rice flour and soy flour, free of dairy, egg, wheat and white sugar.
